thesis: China's manufacturing dominance survives rising wages not because of cheap labor but because of an ecosystem density that no tariff cycle can replicate.
stakes: Every politician promising to bring manufacturing home is either ignorant of what actually makes China competitive or betting you won't notice. Your tax dollars and consumer prices depend on understanding the real machinery.
counterpoint: The ecosystem advantage is partly engineered through state subsidies and export-tax rebates that distort true costs, and the lowest-value manufacturing is already leaving China for Vietnam and Bangladesh.
implication: If you build, source, or vote on trade policy without understanding cluster density, you are operating on a story about wages that was already obsolete a decade ago.
close: So the next time someone tells you they will bring the factories back with a tariff, ask them how they plan to rebuild thirty years of supply chain gravity in a political cycle. The 15-cent miracle was never about the 15 cents. It was about the city you have to become to make it possible. Geography is a tool, not a cage, and right now one city is using it better than everyone else.
